Consider a login plus a single add-candidate/open-job CRUD screen backed by SQLite, with correct 403s for the Observer and no moves, conversations or live updates. It passes both gates. It can plausibly earn hro_job_open (1), hro_add_candidate (1) and hro_add_email_rules (1). It can also earn hro_refusal_status (1), because that row counts only replays that were refused, and an Observer add-candidate or open-job replay refused with 403 satisfies it. That is about 4/61 = 0.066 functional, above the 0.05 floor. Rows that need a move, multi-card move or undo control (hro_observer_readonly, hro_anonymous, hro_candidate_no_staff) and hro_restart (which needs seeded notes, messages, unread counts and activity) should fail. With visual Likert scores of about 2-3 on a board-only UI and polish at 0, the reward is roughly 0.6*0.066 + 0.2*(0.25 to 0.5) = 0.09 to 0.14. Without the refusal_status point the stub falls to 3/61 = 0.049, below the floor, and earns 0. This is partial credit for real partial work against a golden near 1.0, so the task still clearly separates a real build from a stub, and it is not a row-7 defect. It is noted because the stub could land at the bottom of the 0.1-0.7 target band. Conforming-alternative probe: no conforming app fails because of what the brief asks. Routes, labels and layout are explicitly left to the builder (hireops_rules.md preamble; instruction.md: 'layout and names are yours'), so this row does not penalize any valid design.

Unread expectations are state-relative where state can move: Rafael's count uses deltas ('rises by exactly two'), and Mei's count is 'computed from the observed sequence' (judge.toml hro_unread_counts; prompt.md:49), so a staff Conversations view that auto-opens a conversation is tolerated. Polish says 'Never use Lena Fischer's conversation', gates open no conversation, and visual only views as Noor. hro_restart compares against a pre-restart baseline (lesson 16). The client catch-up after a 409 is a display update, not a change. 'Adding a note doesn't count' is honoured by B(12). Ingrid reopens Interview and Offer rejections only to their own stages, and her refused reopen is a role refusal (hro_mgr_early_refused), not a wrong-target probe. Observer and candidate accounts as manager are never tried. Probes are distinctive: every job/card/name is suffixed per review (functional/prompt.md:15), timed-action messages get unique suffixes (line 21), and seeded probes match seed_data.json exactly (Platform Engineer Applied Greta Lindqvist/Ade Bello/Marco Rossi positions 1-3, Screen Priya Nair/Samuel Ortiz; APP-101 note 'Strong systems answers; weaker on incident follow-up.'; Lena APP-301 has 3 messages with read_count 2 -> 1 unread; Noor APP-101 has 120 messages numbered '(#001)'.., so hro_thread_latest/earlier are decidable by number). Lessons 7/14 (repeat and void handling for timed steps) are defined once and apply to every timed leg (functional/prompt.md:21, polish/prompt.md:18): t0 after the trigger succeeds, 500 ms polling, void only before t0 or on a failed trigger, at most two repeats, met=false never repeated, all-void fails. Lesson 15: protocol D (prompt.md:59) records jobs, per-stage order, notes, last messages, unread counts and activity, calls restart_app and re-reads all in a fresh context. Refusal rows require server observation by replay (line 31); statuses are explicit (hro_refusal_status); focus is measured as document.activeElement (hro_refused_put_back, polish rows); scroll anchor as getBoundingClientRect().top (hro_pol_earlier_place).

DEFECT (blocking): the generic negative-leg rule in tests/scored/functional/prompt.md:21 reads: 'For a step whose expected result is that something does not change or does not appear (still not seen, a count that does not rise, a place that does not move), the forbidden change is the watched condition: keep reading for the full 15000 ms, pass that leg only if it never appeared, then reload that page once and confirm it is still absent.' The only functional leg that is 'a place that does not move' is hro_unread_scrolled_up (functional/judge.toml:349-357; protocol U at prompt.md:49: 'as Rafael scroll up to earlier messages, then as Noor ... send a message; read Rafael's place, the notice and the unread count before and after he goes to it'). The mandated reload makes this leg undecidable or wrongly failed for a conforming app: after a reload the brief requires the conversation to open on its most recent 30 messages scrolled to the newest (hireops_rules.md:150-151), so the scrolled-up place is necessarily gone, and having the conversation open at its newest counts as reading (hireops_rules.md:157-158), so the new message is read before 'he goes to it', destroying the criterion's 'stays unread until he goes to it, then it is read' leg and the protocol's 'before and after he goes to it' readings. The golden behaves exactly so: threads.js:7 restores the open thread from storage on load, and open() at threads.js:120-131 calls toBottom() and then markRead(id). A literal judge therefore fails the reference on hro_unread_scrolled_up (weight 2 of 61 functional weight, about 2% of total reward) or must improvise; the outcome is not decidable from the rubric as written. No configured judge run exists (raw-evidence-index scope: full configured grading absent), so this is NOT EXERCISED, not refuted.

NOTES (non-blocking, P3): (a) Protocol K (prompt.md:51) rejects Tomas's card so hro_candidate_private can check that no candidate response contains 'a rejection reason', but the reason text is not required to be distinctive or suffixed (line 15 suffixes titles and names only); a natural reason such as 'Not moving forward' collides with the candidate wording for Rejected (seed candidate_status_labels), making that leak check ambiguous. (b) hro_pol_earlier_place (polish/judge.toml:42-44) says scroll to the top, note the top message and its position, then bring in earlier messages; with a conforming auto-load-on-scroll implementation (the brief only says 'lets me pull in earlier ones') the load can fire before the anchor is recorded, and no wait-until-loaded condition is given. Both are decidable by a careful judge. Other negative legs under the same rule (hro_seen 'still not seen' after the Observer, hro_unread_counts 'count does not rise') survive a reload of Rafael's page and are not defects. Visual likert rows are craft judgements with anchors and are out of scope for outcome-based binary wording.
unresolved.counterexample: Conforming app (the golden itself): Rafael scrolls up in Noor's conversation and Noor sends a message; within 15 s the app shows a one-new-message notice, keeps Rafael's place and leaves the conversation unread. Following functional/prompt.md:21 literally ('a place that does not move' is a negative leg), the judge watches 15 s, then reloads Rafael's page; the app reopens the conversation at the newest message (threads.js:7, 120-131; required by hireops_rules.md:150-151) and marks it read. The judge sees the place moved and the message already read before Rafael 'goes to it' and fails hro_unread_scrolled_up, so the reference loses weight 2. Conversely the post-reload check cannot distinguish a broken app that jumps to the newest message on every arrival, since both end at the newest after reload.
unresolved.suggested_fix: In functional/prompt.md:21 remove 'a place that does not move' from the reload-and-confirm rule (or exempt scroll-place legs from the reload), and in protocol U state that Rafael's place and unread count are read in the same timed action after the notice appears plus 2000 ms with no reload before he goes to the new message; optionally require a suffixed rejection reason in protocol K.
